title: How to count cells above the average
task: How many values beat the mean — above-average performers, over-target rows.

excel.note: Concatenate the operator with the computed average. Use >= to include values equal to the mean.

explanation: COUNTIF's criteria can be built on the fly: ">"&AVERAGE(A2:A6) evaluates the average (30 here) and glues it to the greater-than sign, giving the criterion ">30". Two values (40 and 50) exceed the mean, so the count is 2. The & is what lets a criterion reference a calculated value — the same trick works with a cell (">"&C1) or another function (">"&MEDIAN(...)). Excel also has a built-in COUNTIF-style shortcut, but this concatenation pattern is the portable, general way and extends to SUMIF/AVERAGEIF.
